text:
Ellen: Customer reported a burst of streaming failures — they see a bunch of 502s and were billed for tokens even though the client closed the connection early. Can we check?
Mike: Sending the relevant proxy/runtime snippets. Looks like a half-close from client then a runtime write fails (broken pipe) and gateway returns 502. :confused:
Anjali: paste the proxy/ingress trace please, need theTCP sequence.
Mike: log excerpt:
```
[ingress] conn=0x7f14 read EOF (client FIN)
[proxy] proxy->runtime id=rt-03 established
[runtime] attempt to write chunk to client -> write failed: broken pipe
[proxy] upstream connection reset: ECONNRESET
[gateway] response 502
```
Dan: So flow is: client FIN (half-close) -> we still try to stream tokens -> runtime write fails with EPIPE/Broken pipe -> proxy surfaces 502. Our metrics treat that as upstream 5xx and bill.
Ellen: Customer insists it was their client aborting and they shouldn't be billed. We need repro and a classification fix. ops-bot, can you capture an example request id?
ops-bot: created repro ticket req-79312 and captured request ids: r-2026-09, r-2026-10
Mike: quick local repro I used (kill client after first chunk):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate/stream" \
  -d '{"prompt":"long-output","stream":true}' &
sleep 0.8; pkill -9 curl
```
Anjali: On our metrics ~70% of these are client FIN then proxy sees immediate RST to upstream. Classification rule today: any upstream connection failure -> 5xx. That overcounts client aborts.
Dan: Proposal: add heuristic to classify as client_abort (exclude billing) when we observe: client FIN before any final chunk + proxy record of "write to client failed: EPIPE" and no upstream error code from runtime. Need to be careful: if runtime actually crashes and returns 5xx before client FIN we must still bill.
Mike: I'll attach pcap and full logs for the two request ids. Also include the chunked-encoding headers we saw: 
```
Transfer-Encoding: chunked\nContent-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8\n
```
We occasionally see incomplete chunk trailers which complicates detection.
Ellen: Support runbook items: (1) if customer reports streaming missing final tokens, ask for client logs and time; (2) ask for request-id and we check proxy trace for client FIN vs runtime 5xx; (3) if client FIN first -> refund and mark as client_abort; (4) escalate to billing if >$X in charges.
Anjali: I'll open a follow-up ticket to change classification and add a small retrospective test in staging to simulate half-close + immediate RST.
Dan: Note: need a regression test where runtime legitimately fails mid-stream (OOM/crash) to ensure we still count those as upstream 5xx.
Ellen: Thanks — please post updates here and tag #billing-escalation when we get a fix or refunds processed.
